newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung in talks for Ssangyong Motor - paper.
newsitem.headline: Samsung in talks for Ssangyong Motor - paper.

text.p: South Korea's giant Samsung Group has entered into negotiations with Ssangyong Group over the takeover of Ssangyong Motor Co, the Chosun Ilbo newspaper reported on Sunday.
The newspaper quoted unnamed sources at Ssangyong Group as saying a meeting between the two groups was held in mid-September at a hotel in central Seoul to discuss the deal.
It said Samsung had earlier held discussions with Germany's Mercedes-Benz AG, part of Daimler-Benz AG, on forming a technical tie-up.
Mercedes-Benz, which has a five percent stake in Ssangyong Motor, and Samsung also discussed at those meetings a Samsung takeover of Ssangyong Motor, the newspaper reported.
Officials at Samsung and Ssangyong groups were not immediately available for comment, but an industry source said on Sunday the report was "believed to have some ground".
Samsung Group formed a technical tie-up with Nissan Motor Co of Japan and established Samsung Motors Inc in order to enter the already crowded passenger car industry from 1998.
However, the Chosun Ilbo report said the technology transfer from Nissan had not been smooth and Samsung had started looking for another partner.
In the case of Ssangyong Group, the accumulating losses at the four-wheel drive maker have led it to consider seeking a new owner, the Chosun Ilbo said.
Ssangyong Motor posted a net loss of 126.22 billion won in calendar 1995 on a 986.74 billion won turnover, compared with a 79.32 billion loss on 805.93 billion won turnover in 1994.
